dialogue_history.content: Should “very risky” use the High-Risk Patient definition (suicide risk High or Severe, or PHQ-9 > 15, or GAD-7 > 15), or a different rule?

The term “very risky patients” is defined as patients meeting the High Severity, High Risk Patient Group criteria: either a PHQ-9 depression score greater than 19 or a GAD-7 anxiety score greater than 14, combined with a suicide risk level of High or Severe. It does not use PHQ-9 > 15 or GAD-7 > 15 thresholds.
What audit table name and columns should I create, and what timestamp and reason text should each record contain (is this a one-time insert, or should future encounters also be logged automatically)?

The audit table should be named `high_risk_encounter_audit` and include columns for an auto-generated audit ID, the encounter key, patient key, clinician ID, facility ID, an audit timestamp (defaulting to the current time), and a reason field. Each inserted record should capture the current timestamp automatically and use the reason text 'High Severity and High Suicide Risk'. This is a one-time insert based on the current data snapshot; the statement does not set up automatic logging for future encounters.

Should I log only encounters whose linked assessment meets the risk rule, or every encounter of any patient who has at least one qualifying assessment? Are the audit column names audit_id, enckey, patkey, clinid, facid, audit_timestamp, and reason acceptable?

For the first part: the audit should log only encounters whose linked assessment meets the risk rule (i.e., the encounter's own assessment satisfies the high depression/anxiety threshold AND high/severe suicide risk), not every encounter belonging to a patient who has any qualifying assessment elsewhere.

For the second part: yes, the column names audit_id, enckey, patkey, clinid, facid, audit_timestamp, and reason are acceptable.
